parsed.draft_response:
Thanks for reporting this—sorry for the impact to your operations team. A jump from ~under 5 seconds to ~30–45 seconds after the last release is a significant regression.

We’ve escalated this to our engineering team to investigate. To help them narrow down what changed and where the time is being spent, could you share the following:
1) The date/time (and release version/build if available) of the “last release.”
2) Whether the slowdown is on the entire analytics dashboard or only specific pages/views.
3) How you’re measuring the 30–45 seconds (e.g., time to first render, time to fully interactive, or time until the data finishes loading).
4) Any browser/client details for affected users (browser + version, and whether it’s consistent across all users/locations).
5) If possible, a screenshot or a short copy of any errors you see during the slow load, plus any relevant logs/console/network info.

Once we have these, we’ll continue the investigation and update you on our findings.
promised_actions: We will escalate this performance regression to our engineering team for investigation.
We will review additional details you provide (timing, affected pages, and measurable metrics) to narrow down what changed after the last release.
safety_notes: Customer reports a post-release performance regression (under 5s to 30–45s). Human review/engineering escalation is needed and cannot be resolved or root-caused here.
Requesting minimal additional details (release version/date, which pages/features, metric definition, and any logs/screenshots) to proceed.
